chosen.premise: Pidgeotto immobilizes prey with its claws, then carries it more than 60 miles back to its nest.
chosen.hook: Pidgeotto can take immobilized prey on a 60-mile flight home.
chosen.visualIdea: A map route stretches 60+ miles as Pidgeotto flies overhead carrying an Exeggcute-shaped silhouette.
chosen.note: A highly specific, unsettling mechanic backed by three Pokédex entries; the 60-mile map and immobilized prey make the premise immediately visual.

candidates.premise: Pidgeotto is a 1.1-meter, 30-kilogram Bird Pokémon that carries prey more than 60 miles.
candidates.hook: This 30-kilo bird can fly prey more than 60 miles home.
candidates.visualIdea: Stat cards show 1.1 m and 30 kg, then a distance counter races past 60 miles beneath a flying Pidgeotto.
candidates.note: The 30-kilogram bird-versus-60-mile contrast is compelling and fully supported, though it overlaps thematically with the stronger delivery mechanic.

candidates.premise: No matter how high it flies, Pidgeotto can still distinguish the movements of its prey below.
candidates.hook: Pidgeotto's vision works from any altitude.
candidates.visualIdea: The camera climbs above clouds, then hard-cuts to Pidgeotto's view tracking tiny movement on the ground.
candidates.note: Strong visual mystery and well supported, but “from any altitude” slightly overstates the source’s hyperbolic wording.

candidates.premise: Pidgeotto constantly circles and patrols a large territory—then shows no mercy to anything that enters it.
candidates.hook: Pidgeotto doesn't just own territory—it patrols it relentlessly.
candidates.visualIdea: A top-down territory circle is repeatedly traced by Pidgeotto before an intruder crosses the boundary.
candidates.note: The patrol-and-punish behavior is well documented, but “large territory” is undefined and the angle is less surprising than the prey-delivery fact.

candidates.premise: Pidgeotto's intruder defense shifts from fierce pecking in Red to sharp-claw punishment in later entries.
candidates.hook: Pidgeotto has two very different ways to evict an intruder.
candidates.visualIdea: A split screen labels one attack 'beak' and the other 'claws' as an intruder crosses a territory line.
candidates.note: The entries do differ, but this may reflect descriptive variation rather than a meaningful two-mode defense system.

candidates.premise: Pidgeotto evolves from Pidgey at level 18, then remains the middle stage until evolving at level 36.
candidates.hook: Pidgeotto's entire evolutionary chapter lasts 18 levels.
candidates.visualIdea: An evolution timeline ticks from Pidgey at 18 through Pidgeotto, ending with Pidgeot at 36.
candidates.note: The 18-level span is concrete and visual, but the supplied research does not actually include Pidgeot’s evolution method at level 36.
